title: Tenant Isolation and Pseudonym Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Learning Record Store
Multi-Tenancy
Student Privacy
Pseudonymization
Learning Analytics
description: A p5.js explorer in which learners derive a learner's pseudonymous key in two school districts with per-district salts or one global salt, see whether an analytics reader can link the keys, and click each level of the tenancy tree to read whether its boundary is hard or soft.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: District tenancy boundaries and per-district salted pseudonymous learner keys
learningObjectives: The learner will explain why a per-district salt gives one learner two unrelated pseudonymous keys, and which boundaries are hard or soft.
prerequisites: The actor account of an xAPI statement (home page and name) (Chapter 16)
The idea of a one-way hash function
The district, school, course and section hierarchy (Chapter 20)

accessibility.notes: Controls are native form elements; hard and soft boundaries are shown by solid versus dashed borders and by text, not by color alone

controls.label: Learner account name
controls.purpose: The account name mixed into each key

controls.label: Per-district salt / One global salt
controls.purpose: Choose how the salt is handled

controls.label: Attacker view
controls.purpose: Hide the vault and show only the analytics side

controls.label: Tenancy tree levels
controls.purpose: Show whether a level's boundary is hard or soft and its rule

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict-then-observe explanation with an adversary's view
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Step-through comparison of two salt policies plus clickable boundary rules
keyQuestions: What does an analytics reader see, and what would let them link two rows to one learner?
Why does deleting a district's salt make its keys underivable?
Which boundaries are enforced by storage keys and which by role-based access control?
commonMisconceptions: A hashed name is anonymous no matter how it is salted
All levels of the tenancy tree are isolated in the same way
The pseudonym alone reveals the learner if you know the hash function
assessmentOpportunities: Explain why per-district salts defeat cross-district linking
Classify each tenancy level as hard or soft and name its enforcement
Explain how erasure by deleting a salt works

equations: student_key = hash(salt | home page | name); FNV-1a stands in for the design's HMAC-SHA256
assumptions: The learner has the same home page and name in both districts, as in the chapter's worked example
limitations: Tokens are illustrative and not cryptographically secure
The identity service and vault are designed, not built
